en: Every business hits the same wall the moment your business outgrows the systems that got you here.
zh: 每一家企业都会撞上同一堵墙——当你的业务超出了带你走到今天的那些系统的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: Spreadsheets everywhere, five different logins, data scattered across entities that don't even talk to each other.
zh: 到处都是电子表格,五个不同的登录账号,数据散落在彼此根本不互通的各个实体之间。

speaker: Unknown
en: If your finance team spends more time finding data than using it, that's when you need the Intuit ERP.
zh: 如果你的财务团队花在找数据上的时间比用数据还多,那就是你需要 Intuit ERP 的时候了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Intuit Enterprise Suite is the AI-native ERP solution that's powerful, painless, and proven, built for businesses scaling fast without the complexity that usually comes with it.
zh: Intuit Enterprise Suite 是 AI 原生的 ERP 解决方案,强大、省心、经过验证,专为快速扩张的企业打造,而没有通常伴随而来的复杂性。

speaker: Unknown
en: From the makers of QuickBooks, learn more at intuit.com slash ERP.
zh: 出自 QuickBooks 的缔造者,请访问 intuit.com/ERP 了解更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI is full of possibilities.
zh: AI 充满了可能性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Enterprises run on realities.
zh: 而企业靠现实运转。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why PEGA combines the world's most powerful AI with the governance, transparency, and control enterprises demand.
zh: 这就是为什么 PEGA 将世界上最强大的 AI 与企业所要求的治理、透明度和控制力相结合。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can move faster, adapt faster, and scale AI with confidence.
zh: 让你行动更快、适应更快,并充满信心地扩展 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: All the power of AI, none of the uncertainty.
zh: 拥有 AI 的全部力量,而没有不确定性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Learn more at PEGA.com slash AI.
zh: 请访问 PEGA.com/AI 了解更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: This guy said, we're looking for people who have absolutely no experience in television.
zh: 这个人说,我们寻找的是在电视行业完全没有经验的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which I was like, wow.
zh: 我当时心想,哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: I said, they didn't even have television where I've been living.
zh: 我说,我住的地方连电视都没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I'm walking around in flip flops and pajamas for eight years.
zh: 我是说,八年来我一直穿着人字拖和睡衣到处走。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was hard to believe now, but MTV was really revolutionary at the time.
zh: 现在很难相信,但 MTV 在当时确实是革命性的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a sign of some kind of future that might be coming.
zh: 它是某种可能即将到来的未来的一个标志。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is Masters of Scale.
zh: 这是 Masters of Scale。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Jeff Berman, your host.
zh: 我是 Jeff Berman,你的主持人。

speaker: Unknown
en: This week on the show, the word legend gets thrown around a lot.
zh: 本周节目中,“传奇”这个词被用得很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: In this case, we have a legend who is actually legendary, Tom Preston.
zh: 而在这个例子里,我们有一位真正名副其实的传奇人物,Tom Preston。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tom is a co-founder of MTV, former CEO of Viacom, and his new memoir, Unplugged, is full of wild stories and deeply meaningful lessons from his life as an unconventional CEO.
zh: Tom 是 MTV 的联合创始人、Viacom 的前 CEO,他的新回忆录《Unplugged》充满了他在作为一位非传统 CEO 的人生中那些狂野的故事和深刻而有意义的教训。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is gonna be a fun one.
zh: 这期会很有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tom, welcome to Masters of Scale.
zh: Tom,欢迎来到 Masters of Scale。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nice to be here.
zh: 很高兴来到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Great to have you here.
zh: 很荣幸请你来。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was in an airport with a book that I wasn't really loving.
zh: 我当时在机场,手里拿着一本我并不怎么喜欢的书。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I popped into the airport bookstore.
zh: 于是我走进了机场书店。

speaker: Unknown
en: I saw your book.
zh: 我看到了你的书。

speaker: Unknown
en: I figured I'll grab that.
zh: 我想着就拿一本吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll start it on the plane.
zh: 上飞机后开始读。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fortunately, there was no Wi-Fi on the plane.
zh: 幸运的是,飞机上没有 Wi-Fi。

speaker: Unknown
en: By the time I landed on a cross-country flight, I'd nearly finished it.
zh: 等我落地时,一趟横跨全国航班下来,我几乎读完了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is a rollicking read.
zh: 这是一本让人读得酣畅淋漓的书。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the things that stood out for me in reading the book
zh: 在读这本书的过程中,有一点让我印象特别深刻,

speaker: Unknown
en: was the extent to which the early part of your career was shaped by breaking rules, making new rules.
zh: 那就是你职业生涯的早期在很大程度上是被打破规则、制定新规则所塑造的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as we look at what's happening in the world today, I'm curious what your take is on what the line is between what is acceptable rule-breaking and what is really reckless and dangerous rule-breaking.
zh: 而当我们看看当今世界正在发生的事情时,我很好奇,你如何看待“可以接受地打破规则”与“真正鲁莽而危险的打破规则”之间的界限在哪里。

speaker: Unknown
en: First of all, I'm excited to hear that they were selling my book in a bookstore in the airport, and I'm glad you liked it.
zh: 首先,听到他们在机场书店里卖我的书,我很兴奋,而且很高兴你喜欢它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, in terms of breaking rules, well, you don't want to break rules that are against the law, generally.
zh: 嗯,关于打破规则嘛,一般来说,你不会想去打破违法的规则。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, a lot of the rules that we broke, say, with MTV, they were more in the cultural realm.
zh: 你知道,我们打破的很多规则,比如说和 MTV 一起打破的那些,更多是在文化层面的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we broke rules on a business basis.
zh: 而且我们是在商业基础上打破规则的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, we, at one point, couldn't get the cable operators.
zh: 比如,我们一度拿不下有线电视运营商。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who were at that point in time in the early eighties, it seems like ancient history, but they were local monopolists.
zh: 他们当时,也就是八十年代初,听起来像远古历史了,但他们是地方垄断者。

speaker: Unknown
en: We decided after a couple of years, and we only had a couple of million subscribers, we would just go over their heads.
zh: 几年后,当我们只有几百万订户时,我们决定直接越过头去找用户。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was like, screw them.
zh: 就是那种,去他们的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we cranked up the I Want My MTV campaign, which to try and pull, you know, demand right through these distributors who were largely Elvis fans.
zh: 于是我们发起了 I Want My MTV(我要我的 MTV)运动,试图直接从那些基本是猫王粉丝的分销商手中拉动需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who didn't like MTV, who didn't like the idea of paying us 10 cents a month.
zh: 他们不喜欢 MTV,不喜欢每月付我们 10 美分这个主意。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were just somebody who cut into their profit margins.
zh: 在他们眼里,我们就是个蚕食他们利润率的家伙。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that was a rule broken, which was like, it was sort of not a polite thing to do in the cable business back then.
zh: 所以那是一次打破规则,在当年的有线电视行业里,这种做法有点不太体面。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, and beyond that, let's go back to Hindu Kush, which, I mean, I think most people know you for MTV, such an iconic stretch of your career.
zh: 嗯,除此之外,让我们回到兴都库什,我是说,我想大多数人是通过 MTV 认识你的,那是你职业生涯中如此具有标志性的一段。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you started by building an apparel brand out of India, right?
zh: 但你最初是在印度做服装品牌的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And Afghanistan.
zh: 还有阿富汗。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, there were not a lot of rules.
zh: 是啊，那时没那么多规矩。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wanted to live there.
zh: 我想住在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had been traveling and I had developed this fascination with that part of the world.
zh: 我一直在旅行，对世界的那个地方产生了迷恋。

speaker: Unknown
en: I figured, how can I afford to live here?
zh: 我琢磨着，我怎么能负担得起住在这里呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: I need to start a business because I couldn't get a job.
zh: 我需要创业，因为我找不到工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I started this business in the garment business, knowing nothing, never wanting to be in the garment business, but it took off like a rocket.
zh: 于是我在服装行业做起了这门生意，一无所知，也从没想进入服装行业，但它像火箭一样腾飞了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was highly enjoyable for a bunch of years.
zh: 有好几年都是非常愉快的经历。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then at the end, there was an embargo that Jimmy Carter put down that ultimately put my company out of business.
zh: 而到最后，吉米·卡特颁布了一项禁运令，最终让我的公司倒闭了。

speaker: Unknown
en: No more imports from India.
zh: 不再允许从印度进口。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I sent three tons of clothes to Montreal and we smuggled them over the St. Lawrence Seaway, which was insane.
zh: 我把三吨衣服运到蒙特利尔，然后我们通过圣劳伦斯航道把它们偷运过去，那简直是疯狂。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know what I was thinking, but I was kind of just looking for a little justice.
zh: 我不知道我当时在想什么，但我大概只是想寻求一点公正。

speaker: Unknown
en: You had a business that was growing.
zh: 你有一个正在成长的生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: You were
zh: 你当时

speaker: Unknown
en: Living the entrepreneur's dream and really, and the stories are so colorful and so vivid.
zh: 过着创业者的梦想生活，真的，而且那些故事是那么丰富多彩、那么鲜活。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then all of a sudden you've got a change in geopolitics.
zh: 然后突然之间，地缘政治发生了变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've got a rise in tariffs.
zh: 关税上升了。

speaker: Unknown
en: This sounds very familiar.
zh: 这听起来非常眼熟。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And was paying attention to the news today.
zh: 而且我今天一直在关注新闻。

speaker: Unknown
en: I really feel for all these young importers these days who are screwed.
zh: 我真的很心疼如今这些被坑惨了的年轻进口商。

speaker: Unknown
en: What did you learn from then that would be useful for those entrepreneurs today who are dealing with the similar turmoil?
zh: 你从那时学到的东西，对今天那些正应对类似动荡的创业者会有什么帮助？

speaker: Unknown
en: I've learned humility.
zh: 我学会了谦逊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Living in that part of the world, you learn humility and you also build up a great confidence in yourself and your ability to do things.
zh: 生活在世界的那个地方，你学会谦逊，同时你也会建立起对自己以及自己做事能力的巨大信心。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, as I always say, it was like a sort of a bebop business lifestyle.
zh: 你知道，就像我常说的，那有点像一种 bebop 式的生意与生活方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: You would improvise, you would take chances, you would take risks, you would bet on unusual people, you would learn how to tolerate unusual people.
zh: 你会即兴发挥，你会抓机会，你会冒险，你会押注不寻常的人，你会学会容忍不寻常的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of this kind of came in place and it made sort of a perfect resume for someone who was going to lead what became a cutting edge
zh: 所有这一切综合在一起，构成了对某些人来说堪称完美的履历——那些要领导一家后来成为前沿

speaker: Unknown
en: Eccentric media company.
zh: 特立独行的媒体公司的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there are so many ambitious 20-somethings who are terrified of stepping off of the well-worn path.
zh: 我认为有很多雄心勃勃的二十多岁的年轻人，害怕离开那条走惯了的老路。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're kind of going through a machine of, well, it's the right college and maybe it's the right grad school or the job at the right company.
zh: 他们有点像在通过一台机器运转，嗯，要上对的大学，也许还要上对的研究生院，或者去对的公司工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's real fear about following something that's more of a passion or that they feel in their body just might be something worth trying and being a little bit more beboppy about their career.
zh: 而对于追随某种更出于热情的东西——或者他们内心真切地觉得也许值得尝试的东西——存在着真实的恐惧，对自己的职业更 bebop 一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you're talking with young people who are in that mindset, how are you helping them understand that there's another path?
zh: 当你和处于那种心态的年轻人交谈时，你是如何帮助他们理解还有另一条路的？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a tougher time for kids.
zh: 现在对孩子们来说是更艰难的时期。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, you're in your 20s these days.
zh: 你知道，如今你二十多岁。

speaker: Unknown
en: You want to start a career.
zh: 你想开启一份事业。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the office culture thing has sort of collapsed.
zh: 而办公室文化那套东西有点崩塌了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of things that maybe we knew when we were that age are sort of gone.
zh: 很多我们那个年纪可能知道的东西，差不多都消失了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But, you know, step off the conveyor belt and embrace some uncertainty.
zh: 但是，你知道，离开那条传送带，拥抱一些不确定性吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: No one's going to miss you if you're gone for a while.
zh: 你消失一段时间，没有人会想念你。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can maybe travel all around the world like I did.
zh: 你也许可以像我一样环游世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I would say that travel...
zh: 但我想说，旅行……

speaker: Unknown
en: Making that part of your post-college experiences is like the world's greatest classroom.
zh: 把它作为你大学毕业后的经历的一部分，就像世界上最伟大的课堂。

speaker: Unknown
en: You learn a lot about empathy.
zh: 你会学到很多关于同理心的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: You learn a lot about your country.
zh: 你会学到很多关于你的国家的知识。

speaker: Unknown
en: You learn a lot about yourself.
zh: 你会学到很多关于你自己的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you come back, you're probably going to be more attractive to someone who's a recruiter than someone who just went on the conveyor belt the whole time.
zh: 而且当你回来时，比起那些从头到尾都待在传送带上的人，你可能对招聘者更有吸引力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Relax, for God's sake.
zh: 放轻松，看在上帝的份上。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you came back, you ultimately answered an ad.
zh: 当你回来时，你最终回应了一则广告。

speaker: Unknown
en: That wanted people to work at a fledgling TV network who had no TV experience.
zh: 那则广告想招募没有任何电视经验的人去一家初创的电视网络工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had come back.
zh: 我回来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had built this business.
zh: 我建起了这门生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a multimillion dollar business.
zh: 那是一门数百万美元的生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a big success, which I never expected.
zh: 它是个巨大的成功,这是我从未预料到的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I loved it.
zh: 而且我爱它。

speaker: Unknown
en: It crashed and burned.
zh: 它崩塌烧毁了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm deep and dead.
zh: 我深陷谷底,死气沉沉。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm back in New York.
zh: 我回到了纽约。

speaker: Unknown
en: All my friends, I'm now 33, all my friends have gone out and they got married.
zh: 我所有的朋友,我当时 33 岁,我所有的朋友都出去结婚了。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have careers.
zh: 他们都有了自己的事业。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I said, what the hell am I gonna do?
zh: 我说,我到底要干什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: I bought this book, What Color Is Your Parachute?
zh: 我买了这本书,《你的降落伞是什么颜色?》

speaker: Unknown
en: The only self-help book I've ever bought.
zh: 这是我唯一买过的自助书。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've recommended it to so many people.
zh: 我把它推荐给了很多人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it said that you have transferable skills.
zh: 我是说,书里说你拥有可迁移的技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can do a lot of different things.
zh: 你可以做很多不同的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you, by the way, you should do something that you love.
zh: 而且顺便说一句,你应该做你热爱的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what do you love?
zh: 那你热爱什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: So they had all these little exercises where you could evaluate your skills, look at what you like.
zh: 书里有很多小练习,让你评估自己的技能,看看自己喜欢什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I came up with like music.
zh: 我得出的结果是类似音乐。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I was a music nut.
zh: 我是说,我是个音乐迷。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I saw this article in Billboard Magazine by this guy, John Lackey, was interviewed and he was talking about this was the start of cable TV.
zh: 然后我在《公告牌》杂志上看到一篇这个叫 John Lackey 的人的采访文章,他在讲那是有线电视的开端。

speaker: Unknown
en: They had started the movie channel and Nickelodeon and they had plans to start a video music channel.
zh: 他们已经开办了电影频道和 Nickelodeon,并且计划开办一个视频音乐频道。

speaker: Unknown
en: I said, oh God, that's a great idea.
zh: 我说,哦天哪,这主意太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do I get to meet this guy?
zh: 我怎么才能见到这个人?

speaker: Unknown
en: So my brother who was in the record business knew a guy who had just gotten to work there.
zh: 我在唱片行业工作的哥哥认识一个刚去那里工作的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I got an interview and when I went in,
zh: 我得到了一次面试机会,当我走进去的时候,

speaker: Unknown
en: This guy said, we're looking for people who have absolutely no experience in television, which I was like, wow.
zh: 这个人说,我们找的是在电视行业完全没有经验的人,我当时想,哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: I said, they didn't even have television where I've been living.
zh: 我说,我住的地方连电视都没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I'm walking around in flip-flops and pajamas for eight years.
zh: 我是说,我八年来都穿着人字拖和睡衣到处走。

speaker: Unknown
en: So everyone they hired had no experience.
zh: 所以他们雇的每个人都没有经验。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of people came out of radio, came out of the music business.
zh: 很多人来自广播行业,来自音乐行业。

speaker: Unknown
en: In Nickelodeon, they were schoolteachers.
zh: 在 Nickelodeon,他们原本是学校老师。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that turned out to be like the brightest move because we had to think of totally new ways to do things.
zh: 结果这成了最聪明的一步棋,因为我们不得不用全新的方式来做事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's nothing like having no money to force people to innovate.
zh: 而没有什么比没有钱更能逼人创新了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you're working with a group of people who are on a crusade like you are, really passionate about something, you'll figure some good things out.
zh: 如果你和一群像你一样在打一场圣战的人一起工作,对某件事真正充满热情,你们会想出一些好东西来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was hard to believe now, but MTV was really revolutionary at the time.
zh: 现在很难相信,但 MTV 在当时确实是革命性的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a sign of some kind of future that might be coming, this TV revolution.
zh: 它是某种可能即将到来的未来的标志,这场电视革命。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, it's such an interesting challenge, Tom, because you're launching a television network in a world where there are rules and there are norms, right?
zh: 嗯,这是一个非常有趣的挑战,Tom,因为你是在一个有规则、有规范的世界里推出一个电视网络,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: How did MTV thread the needle of taking the experience and expertise of people who knew how the system worked, but the insurgent challenger mindset of the outsiders who came in with the real passion for music and for the artists and the
zh: MTV 是怎么在两者之间穿针引线的:一方面是了解这个系统如何运作的人的经验和专业知识,另一方面是那些带着对音乐和艺人的真正热情进来的局外人的反叛者挑战者心态,

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, screw the rules.
zh: 你知道,去他的规则。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's not do illegal stuff necessarily, but let's do things really differently.
zh: 不一定非要做违法的事,但让我们把事情做得截然不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels like that's a bit of a clash between mindset and culture.
zh: 感觉这有点像是心态和文化之间的冲突。

speaker: Unknown
en: How'd you guys navigate that?
zh: 你们是怎么应对的?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, we had to learn what the business was.
zh: 嗯,我们得先弄清楚这个生意是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, ultimately, the business of cable programming wasn't that complicated.
zh: 你知道,归根结底,有线节目编排这门生意并没有那么复杂。

speaker: Unknown
en: You gotta have to create 168 hours of programming a week.
zh: 你必须每周创作 168 小时的节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're gonna bounce it off a satellite that's 25,000 miles in the sky, which seemed to me like, wow, this is like outer space stuff.
zh: 你要把它发射到 25,000 英里高空的卫星上再反弹下来,这对我来说简直像,哇,这就像外太空的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the future.
zh: 这就是未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which gave you the ultimate scale of, you know, you put together this thing and then it's, you know, it has a footprint all over the United States.
zh: 这给了你终极的规模,你知道的,你把这个东西做出来,然后它,你知道的,它的覆盖范围遍布全美国。

speaker: Unknown
en: We hired people who knew how to do video and we would reach out, say, to NASA.
zh: 我们雇了懂视频的人，然后我们会去联系，比如说，NASA。

speaker: Unknown
en: We would grab a lot of footage that was available in the public domain and utilize that like the rocket ship launches.
zh: 我们会抓取大量公有领域的素材来使用，比如火箭发射。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we got this product from the program staple at the beginning were these music videos which already had been produced.
zh: 而我们一开始节目里的主打产品，就是这些已经制作好的音乐视频。

speaker: Unknown
en: So sort of, we were sort of like a radio station.
zh: 所以某种程度上，我们有点像一个广播电台。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everybody was in their 20s but me.
zh: 除了我，所有人都是二十几岁。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was the oldest guy at 33.
zh: 我是年纪最大的，33 岁。

speaker: Unknown
en: My boss, Bob Pittman, who's a credible character, he was like 26.
zh: 我的老板 Bob Pittman,一个很了不起的人物，当时大概 26 岁。

speaker: Unknown
en: He never went to college, you know, very successful guy.
zh: 他从没上过大学，你知道，是个非常成功的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I learned a lot from him.
zh: 我从他身上学到很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was like a mentor to me.
zh: 他有点像我的导师。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's a great lesson you learned from Bob?
zh: 你从 Bob 身上学到的最重要的经验是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: The key of the business is the consumer.
zh: 生意的核心是消费者。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to deal with a lot of different groups, advertisers, in our case, cable operators, artists, record companies, this and that.
zh: 你必须应付很多不同的群体，广告主，在我们的例子中还有有线电视运营商、艺人、唱片公司，等等等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you could...
zh: 但是如果你能……

speaker: Unknown
en: Make a connection with the consumer and know what's going on inside that consumer's head and maybe build up a research enterprise that gives you a lot of insights into what's going on and get that bond and build up some loyalty.
zh: 与消费者建立连接，了解那个消费者脑袋里在想什么，也许再建立一个研究体系，让你对正在发生的事情有很多洞察，从而建立起那种纽带并培养一些忠诚度。

speaker: Unknown
en: That will allow the other things that have to happen in your business, getting distribution, getting advertisers, convincing people to do things, that will allow them to fall into place.
zh: 那么你的生意中必须发生的其他事情，获取发行渠道、获取广告主、说服人们去做事情，就会水到渠成。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's consumer first, second, and third.
zh: 所以消费者是第一、第二和第三位的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Outside of a couple of years at the NFL, I have spent the entirety of my career working for effectively challenger brands, insurgent brands.
zh: 除了在 NFL 的那几年，我整个职业生涯都在为事实上的挑战者品牌、颠覆者品牌工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: You were in my space for a while.
zh: 你曾经在我的领域待过一段时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was, and I'm very keen to talk to you about that.
zh: 是的，而且我非常想和你聊聊那段经历。

speaker: Unknown
en: But one of the challenges when you're scaling an organization that is a challenger brand and has that insurgents mindset is how you keep that culture while you grow.
zh: 但当你在规模化一个挑战者品牌、带有颠覆者心态的组织时，挑战之一是如何在成长过程中保持那种文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really not hard when you're five or 10 or even 20 or 30 people.
zh: 当你有 5 个人、10 个人，甚至 20 或 30 人的时候，这真的不难。

speaker: Unknown
en: You get to 100, 200, 300, and you start to have things literally called divisions, right?
zh: 但当你到了 100、200、300 人，你开始出现字面意义上叫做「部门」的东西，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: You're separating the company.
zh: 你在把公司分隔开。

speaker: Unknown
en: How were you all able to maintain the culture at MTV through that scaling journey?
zh: 在 MTV 的规模化历程中，你们是如何保持文化的？

speaker: Unknown
en: That was a huge challenge, particularly because we wanted to stay sort of on this cutting edge.
zh: 那是一个巨大的挑战，特别是因为我们想保持某种程度的前沿性。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I always thought that...
zh: 所以我一直认为……

speaker: Unknown
en: Having a creative, innovative corporate culture, I almost hate to use the word corporate, would be a big competitive advantage.
zh: 拥有一种有创意、有创新精神的公司文化，我几乎讨厌用「公司」这个词，会是一个很大的竞争优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: We needed to be diverse, which was not something that...
zh: 我们需要多元化，而这并不是……

speaker: Unknown
en: It happened right out of the box.
zh: 这不是一开始就自然具备的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, we started as a lot of, like, white guys.
zh: 我的意思是，我们起步时大部分是，怎么说，白人男性。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, diversity actually came our way, and it was more challenging than I thought it would be, but we were able to pull that off.
zh: 你知道，多元化实际上是后来才出现的，而且比我想象的更有挑战性，但我们做到了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you want a place where people think their opinions get heard, that politics aren't really important, and organizations sort of flat, I would always go out and speak to them and try and reinforce the company values.
zh: 而且你需要一个人们觉得自己的意见有人听、政治斗争不那么重要的地方，组织结构比较扁平，我总是会走出去和大家交流，努力强化公司的价值观。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, we're a creative organization.
zh: 你知道，我们是一个创意型组织。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's okay to take risks.
zh: 承担风险是没问题的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We encourage you to take risks.
zh: 我们鼓励你们承担风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: We tolerate that.
zh: 我们容忍这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want people to be collegial.
zh: 我们希望人们之间有同事般的情谊。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I wanted to have a fun vibe, you know, so we always had parties and get-togethers and socially.
zh: 而且我想要一种有趣的氛围，你知道，所以我们总是有派对、聚会和各种社交活动。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of these things don't happen anymore.
zh: 这些事情有很多如今都不再发生了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've watched sort of the disappearance of office culture in general.
zh: 我目睹了整体上办公室文化的消失。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not that great with the pandemic.
zh: 疫情之后情况并不太好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, people lose opportunities to bump into each other, learn things via osmosis.
zh: 我的意思是，人们失去了彼此偶遇的机会，失去了通过潜移默化学到东西的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mentorship kind of has disappeared in a way.
zh: 导师制在某种程度上也消失了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think it's sort of coming back.
zh: 所以我觉得这种文化正在某种程度回归。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I don't know if it's ever going to be like it was with people working remotely in their underwear, like from some distant location.
zh: 但我不知道它是否还会像从前那样，因为人们穿着内衣在某个遥远的地方远程工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: They should be working in the office in their underwear.
zh: 他们应该穿着内衣在办公室工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was the MTV way.
zh: 那才是 MTV 的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had the worst dress group of people.
zh: 我们拥有一群穿着最糟糕的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: We probably did have people in their underwear.
zh: 我们可能真的有人穿着内衣上班。

speaker: Unknown
en: We didn't have a dress code.
zh: 我们当时没有着装要求。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was only no frontal nudity was our rule.
zh: 我们唯一的规矩就是不能正面裸体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at that point in time, everybody had a dress code.
zh: 而在那个时候，每家公司都有着装要求。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I said, yeah, screw that.
zh: 但我说，去他的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to be in a traditional company.
zh: 我们才不要做一家传统公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I wanted the people in the company
zh: 我想让公司里的人

speaker: Unknown
en: To look like the people I just saw in a subway car.
zh: 看起来就像我刚在地铁车厢里看到的那种人。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other thing is we wouldn't tolerate, you know, bad actors.
zh: 另一件事是，我们不能容忍，你知道的，害群之马。

speaker: Unknown
en: If someone hires somebody who's substandard and they don't work out, that person is likely to hire other people who are along the same lines.
zh: 如果有人招了一个不达标的人，结果干不成事，这个人很可能又会招来类似水平的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're gradually eroding your company's vibe from the inside.
zh: 于是你就从内部一点点侵蚀掉公司的气质。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: B players hire C players and A players hire A players and it's a pretty firm rule.
zh: B 级的人招 C 级的人，A 级的人招 A 级的人，这是一条相当铁的规律。

speaker: Unknown
en: By the way, I never really focused on money when I would address the company at large.
zh: 顺便说一句，当我对全公司讲话时，我从来不把重点放在钱上。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would always talk about our sort of our creative risks and so forth and leave the money stuff aside.
zh: 我总是谈我们的创作风险之类的东西，把钱的事放在一边。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, that was one thing when you were leading and helping lead MTV.
zh: 嗯，那是你在领导并协助领导 MTV 的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's another thing when you're leading and helping lead Viacom itself.
zh: 而当你在领导并协助领导 Viacom 本身时，就是另一回事了。

speaker: Unknown
en: What was different for you going from overseeing one brand to a family of brands that have wildly different cultures?
zh: 从掌管一个品牌到掌管一群文化截然不同的品牌，对你来说有什么不同？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, we had a family of brands in the sense we became a big cable networking operation.
zh: 嗯，从某种意义上说，我们确实拥有一个品牌大家庭，我们成了一个大型的有线电视网络运营集团。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had Nickelodeon.
zh: 我们有 Nickelodeon。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had Comedy Central.
zh: 我们有 Comedy Central。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had VH1.
zh: 我们有 VH1。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had Noggin.
zh: 我们有 Noggin。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had Nick Jr. We had TV Land.
zh: 我们有 Nick Jr.,还有 TV Land。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a country music television.
zh: 还有乡村音乐电视台。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when I ascended to be the CEO, I became the president of Viacom along with Les Moonves.
zh: 所以当我升任 CEO 时，我和 Les Moonves 一起成为了 Viacom 的总裁。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were like a big entertainment conglomerate.
zh: 我们就像一个大型的娱乐集团。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I became co-president with Les.
zh: 我和 Les 成了联席总裁。

speaker: Unknown
en: We got along well.
zh: 我们相处得很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: He had his fiefdom.
zh: 他有他的领地。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had my fiefdom.
zh: 我有我的领地。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then the digital revolution began to hit and break up this ecosystem.
zh: 但后来数字革命开始冲击并瓦解这个生态系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: We survived on the fact that we had this central operation.
zh: 我们能存活下来，靠的是我们拥有这个中心化的运营体系。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were like editors.
zh: 我们就像编辑。

speaker: Unknown
en: We could manage because of scarcity.
zh: 我们之所以能管理，是因为稀缺性。

speaker: Unknown
en: We didn't have to put out a lot of things.
zh: 我们不必推出大量的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now all of a sudden, we've got the internet.
zh: 而现在突然之间，我们迎来了互联网。

speaker: Unknown
en: Still ahead, Tom Freston on what it takes to break through today's fragmented media landscape.
zh: 稍后，Tom Freston 将谈一谈如何在当今碎片化的媒体格局中实现突破。

en: Hey listeners, Bob here.
zh: 嘿，各位听众，我是 Bob。 [[218→238]] 如果你只听 Masters of Scale 上的 Rapid Response,你可能错过了节目的一半，因为每个周五我们都会在 Rapid Response 单独的 feed 里发布第二期 Rapid Response。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you listen to Rapid Response on Masters of Scale, you may be missing half the show because every Friday we release a second Rapid Response exclusively in the Rapid Response feed.
zh: 如果你在 Masters of Scale 上只听 Rapid Response,你可能错过了节目的一半,因为每周五我们会在 Rapid Response 独家发布第二期 Rapid Response。

speaker: Unknown
en: The guests and topics are just as compelling and timely from Ford's CEO to NASA's administrator to the lessons from the Devil Wears Prada.
zh: 嘉宾和话题同样精彩、同样紧扣时事，从 Ford 的 CEO 到 NASA 的局长，再到《穿普拉达的女王》带来的启示。

speaker: Unknown
en: It takes about 10 seconds to find.
zh: 找到它只需要大约 10 秒钟。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just search Rapid Response wherever you listen to podcasts and hit follow to make sure you never miss an episode.
zh: 只需在你收听播客的地方搜索 Rapid Response,然后点击关注，确保你不错过任何一集。

speaker: Unknown
en: I hope to see you there.
zh: 希望在那里见到你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Humans will never be more intelligent than AI.
zh: 人类的智力永远不会超过 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's going to be two types of companies.
zh: 未来将有两类公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are great at AI and those that went out of business because they weren't.
zh: 一类是擅长 AI 的，另一类是因为不擅长而倒闭的。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we build a future that is human-centered?
zh: 我们如何构建一个以人为本的未来？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Rana Elkayubi, and on my podcast, Pioneers of AI, we answer that question and so many more.
zh: 我是 Rana Elkayubi,在我的播客 Pioneers of AI 中，我们会回答这个问题以及更多其他问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: As an AI scientist, entrepreneur, and investor, I know what it takes to build AI that works for everyone.
zh: 作为一名 AI 科学家、创业者和投资人，我知道构建对每个人都有用的 AI 需要什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every week, I sit down with the pioneers shaping our future, and we take you behind the scenes of the AI that's transforming our lives.
zh: 每周，我都会与塑造我们未来的先驱者坐下来交流，带你走进正在改变我们生活的 AI 的幕后。

speaker: Unknown
en: Find Pioneers of AI wherever you tune in.
zh: 你可以在任何收听平台找到《Pioneers of AI》。

speaker: Unknown
en: Welcome back to Masters of Scale.
zh: 我的意思是,因为那是孩子、青少年、年轻人,他们是最早真正深入互联网、并开始把一部分观看时间和注意力转移到那里的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can find this conversation and more on our YouTube channel and check out the link in the show notes to subscribe to our newsletter.
zh: 你可以在我们的 YouTube 频道找到这段对话及更多内容,并查看节目笔记中的链接订阅我们的通讯。

speaker: Unknown
en: Viacom did not really make that digital leap.
zh: Viacom 并没有真正完成那次数字化转型。

speaker: Unknown
en: It struggled to.
zh: 它转型得很艰难。

speaker: Unknown
en: So given that talent that was there, what stopped you from getting there on the digital side?
zh: 那么考虑到当时拥有的人才,是什么阻碍了你们在数字业务上走到那一步?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, it's back to the innovator's dilemma.
zh: 嗯,这又要回到创新者的窘境了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll just take it in the case of MTV.
zh: 我就以 MTV 为例来说吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: It wasn't like we didn't see what was coming.
zh: 并不是我们没有看到即将到来的变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you have to be an idiot not to see that.
zh: 我的意思是,看不到这一点的人肯定是傻子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we were the canary in the coal mine.
zh: 而我们就是煤矿里的金丝雀。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, because it was kids, teens, young adults, they were the first people to really dive into the internet and begin, you know, moving some of their viewing time and attention over there.
zh: 我是说,因为当时是孩子、青少年、年轻人,他们是最早真正深入互联网、并开始把他们的观看时间和注意力往那边迁移的一批人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, you know, people can upload stuff, share stuff, comment on stuff.
zh: 现在,你知道,人们可以上传东西、分享东西、对东西发表评论。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everybody is almost their own little broadcaster.
zh: 几乎每个人都成了自己的小广播者。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we get in on this business?
zh: 我们怎么才能参与这门生意?

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't really have the DNA to do it.
zh: 我们其实不具备做这件事的 DNA。

speaker: Unknown
en: So all of a sudden now we're probably gonna have to buy something.
zh: 他不想要他的 MTV,而现在他就像—— 他干得还不错。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have to buy something and try and integrate that into our business.
zh: 我们必须买点东西,然后试着把它整合进我们的业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: We bought a bunch of small websites that were of no great consequence, but then met with Mark Zuckerberg.
zh: 我们买了一批没什么重大影响的小网站,但后来见了 Mark Zuckerberg。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll never forget that.
zh: 我永远忘不了那次会面。

speaker: Unknown
en: Someone called me up and they said, you know, we want you to meet this guy, Mark Zuckerberg.
zh: 有人打电话给我说,你知道,我们想让你见见这个人,Mark Zuckerberg。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's like 20 years old.
zh: 他大概 20 岁。

speaker: Unknown
en: He started this thing called The Facebook.
zh: 他创办了一个叫 The Facebook 的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Their revenue's $9 million.
zh: 他们的收入是 900 万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Mark Zuckerberg came in and, you know, we had seen Friendster, been watching MySpace.
zh: 于是 Mark Zuckerberg 进来了,你知道,我们已经见过 Friendster,也一直在关注 MySpace。

speaker: Unknown
en: We saw social media.
zh: 我们看到了社交媒体。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is interesting.
zh: 这很有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: He came in in flip-flops and a hoodie.
zh: 他穿着人字拖和连帽衫进来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: In February in Times Square.
zh: 在二月份,在时代广场。

speaker: Unknown
en: I remember that.
zh: 我记得那件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: There were our offices.
zh: 那是我们的办公室。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they were debating whether to add high school students to the platform.
zh: 他们当时在争论是否要把高中生加入这个平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: We offered to buy the Facebook for a billion and a half dollars, which was a lot for us.
zh: 我们提出用 15 亿美元收购 The Facebook,这对我们来说是一大笔钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, especially with 9 million in revenue.
zh: 嗯,尤其是在只有 900 万美元收入的情况下。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it was a lot for us and half of that would be an earn out.
zh: 是的,这对我们来说是很多钱,而且其中一半会是基于业绩的分期支付。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mark Zuckerberg wanted nothing to do with it.
zh: Mark Zuckerberg 完全不感兴趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: He did not want his MTV and now he's like- He's done okay.
zh: 他不想要他的 MTV,现在他就像—— 他过得挺不错的。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's done all right for himself, that young fellow.
zh: 那个小伙子为自己混得挺好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So then we looked at YouTube.
zh: 然后我们看了 YouTube。

speaker: Unknown
en: YouTube was really like a wow.
zh: YouTube 真的是让人惊叹。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were the king of short-form video and here they are doing this, but it was a whole different model where anybody could upload video, anybody could comment on it and share on it.
zh: 我们当时是短视频领域的王者,而他们在这里做的事情,是一套完全不同的模式,任何人都可以上传视频,任何人都可以对它发表评论并分享。

speaker: Unknown
en: We said, this is fantastic.
zh: 我们说,这太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the problem was because we were a big public company, we were liable.
zh: 所以问题在于,因为我们是一家大型上市公司,我们要承担法律责任。

speaker: Unknown
en: They were people uploading, you know, episodes of our shows or Saturday Night Live, whatever.
zh: 有人在上传,你知道,我们节目的剧集,或者《Saturday Night Live》之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There'd be a lot of copyright stuff.
zh: 那会有很多版权方面的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the board at Viacom viewed it sort of as a copyright infringement machine.
zh: 而 Viacom 的董事会在某种程度上把它看作一台侵犯版权的机器。

speaker: Unknown
en: They ultimately, after I left, sued YouTube famously trying to fight the future.
zh: 在我离开之后,他们最终起诉了 YouTube,出了名地想要对抗未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And no one ever could have imagined the ecosystem that YouTube was ultimately able to put together.
zh: 而当时没有人能想象到 YouTube 最终构建起来的那个生态系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's worth almost $600 billion today.
zh: 我觉得它今天价值将近 6000 亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a monster.
zh: 它是个庞然大物。

speaker: Unknown
en: We cast our eyes on you at MySpace.
zh: 我们把目光投向你在 MySpace 的经历。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's see what's going on over there in Santa Monica.
zh: 我们来看看圣莫尼卡那边在发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's an alternate universe where you would have been my boss, Tom.
zh: 在另一个平行宇宙里,你本来会是我的老板,Tom。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, you open the book with the MySpace story and it sort of being the catalyst for leaving Viacom.
zh: 你知道,你在书的开头讲了 MySpace 的故事,它某种程度上成了你离开 Viacom 的催化剂。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not long after you left, Oprah reached out and asked you to help her build her company.
zh: 你离开后不久,Oprah 联系了你,请你帮她建立她的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's a lesson you learned from working with Oprah that you haven't shared with the world before?
zh: 你从与 Oprah 共事中学到了什么还没和世人分享过的东西?

speaker: Unknown
en: She's the easiest person in the world to talk to, to be with.
zh: 她是全世界最容易交谈、最容易相处的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And she just radiates goodwill and goodness.
zh: 她浑身散发着善意和美好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we all know that.
zh: 这我们都知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: We all know Oprah.
zh: 我们都认识 Oprah。

speaker: Unknown
en: So working with her was a pleasure.
zh: 所以和她共事是一种享受。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oprah had a cadre of largely women who had surrounded her and worked on her syndicated show, which was this huge business.
zh: Oprah 身边有一群主要由女性组成的班底,她们围绕着她,在她的联合播出节目工作,那可是一桩巨大的生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they knew Oprah and they knew what they wanted.
zh: 她们了解 Oprah,也知道自己想要什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they kind of came as outsiders to Hollywood.
zh: 而且她们算是好莱坞的外来者。

speaker: Unknown
en: I helped mostly in the business side.
zh: 我主要在商业方面帮忙。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can we get a deal with Comcast for distribution?
zh: 我们能不能和 Comcast 谈成发行协议?

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we set up some of these departments?
zh: 我们要怎么搭建其中一些部门?

speaker: Unknown
en: I would work on that kind of level.
zh: 我做的就是这一层面的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I did that for a couple of years.
zh: 所以我干了几年。

speaker: Unknown
en: Does what's happening with the consolidation of media and, ironically, then also the fragmentation of media also create lanes for innovation that's exciting?
zh: 媒体的整合,以及讽刺的是随之而来的媒体碎片化,是否也创造了令人兴奋的创新通道?

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm always attracted to stuff around the edges, sort of out of the mainstream.
zh: 我总是被边缘的东西吸引,有点在主流之外的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I look at, like, yeah, the movie business and television, but then I look at 824.
zh: 所以我看,比如,电影行业和电视行业,但接着我看 A24。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're independent.
zh: 他们是独立的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're not owned by one of these public companies, and they've opened up a live venue space.
zh: 他们不被这些上市公司之一所拥有,而且他们开辟了一个现场演出场地。

speaker: Unknown
en: They sell merchandise.
zh: 他们卖周边商品。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have great instincts and great tastes, and they continually seem to pick up and pick projects that are low cost.
zh: 他们有很棒的直觉和很好的品味,而且他们似乎不断地挑选低成本的项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: Seem to do really well at the box office and they're doing television and they're experimenting with shorter form programming that could go on the internet.
zh: 似乎在票房上表现非常出色,他们做电视,还在试验可以放到互联网上的更短形式的节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: I said, well, they're putting together a whole new model.
zh: 我说,好吧,他们正在拼出一个全新的模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I thought one of the most interesting things is the idea that they have a live entertainment venue where they can also test and, you know, sort of pilot things existing outside of the mainstream.
zh: 而且我认为最有趣的一点之一是,他们有一个现场娱乐场地,可以在那里测试、试运行一些存在于主流之外的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: With credibility now.
zh: 而且现在还带着公信力。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think some of these little folks are the people to keep your eye on, some of these people that might jump off YouTube.
zh: 所以我认为这些小人物才是值得关注的人,这些可能从 YouTube 跳出来的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: The YouTube economy is remarkable.
zh: YouTube 经济是非凡的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, one of the most remarkable things about YouTube is YouTube TV as an app.
zh: 我是说,关于 YouTube 最非凡的事情之一,就是 YouTube TV 作为一个应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's like everything we ever wanted.
zh: 那简直就是我们曾经想要的一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, some of this is if you're trying to build something like this, whether it's media or in other categories, what I'm taking from what you're saying is have a point of view.
zh: 我是说,其中一些是,如果你想构建类似这样的东西,无论是媒体还是其他类别,我从你说的这些话里学到的是要有自己的观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Have a point of view and then also build relationships with key creative actors and talent.
zh: 要有自己的观点,并且还要和关键的创意演员与人才建立关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the center of this, all this change, everything is talent.
zh: 在这一切变化的核心,一切都是人才。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's a lot of people today in the YouTube universe and the TikTok universe that you might be able to tap into, have been able to establish pretty amazing businesses.
zh: 今天在 YouTube 宇宙和 TikTok 宇宙里有很多人,你或许可以挖掘,他们已经建立了相当惊人的生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: Speaking of relationships with talent, you've built some pretty incredible ones.
zh: 说到与人才的关系,你建立了一些相当不可思议的关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the secret to building and maintaining relationships with creative talent?
zh: 与创意人才建立和维持关系的秘诀是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: We have to be honest.
zh: 我们必须诚实。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to be someone that they respect, and they need to think that you know what you're doing.
zh: 你必须是他们尊重的人,而且他们需要认为你知道自己在做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Jon Stewart is a perfect example.
zh: Jon Stewart 就是一个完美的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had this guy Craig Kilbourne on The Daily Show.
zh: 我们当时在《每日秀》上有这个人 Craig Kilbourne。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was sort of a middle of the road, kind of a fraternity house guy, nice guy.
zh: 他算是那种中规中矩、兄弟会式的人,一个好人。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we gave Jon Stewart the shot, and he said, I want to do political satire.
zh: 但我们给了 Jon Stewart 这个机会,他说,我想做政治讽刺。

speaker: Unknown
en: We thought something more in the pop culture, but we let John do it.
zh: 我们想的是更偏流行文化的东西,但我们让 Jon 去做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, he invented fake news and it turned into this steamroller full of Emmys and he's hosting the Oscars and he hires Samantha Bee and he hires John Oliver and this whole galaxy of people.
zh: 然后,你知道,他发明了假新闻(fake news),它变成了这台横扫艾美奖的压路机,他去主持奥斯卡,他招了 Samantha Bee,招了 John Oliver,还有这一整个银河系的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: You said that it was harder to diversify MTV than you thought it would be.
zh: 你说过让 MTV 多元化比你预想的更难。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why was it harder and what ultimately worked for you?
zh: 为什么更难,而最终什么对你起了作用?

speaker: Unknown
en: It was harder because I thought, you know, at one point MTV had received a lot of criticism for not airing a black axe, which, you know, fair enough in many ways.
zh: 这更难,因为你知道,有一次 MTV 因为不播放黑人音乐而受到很多批评,这在很多方面来说也确实如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: We kind of came around, we kind of made up for that, and we were the first people to kind of give hip-hop, put it in the living rooms of America.
zh: 我们后来有所转变,算是弥补了这一点,我们是最早把嘻哈音乐带进美国家庭客厅的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, BET or in radio wasn't even playing hip-hop, but...
zh: 我是说,当时连 BET 或电台都不播嘻哈,但是……

speaker: Unknown
en: We were uncomfortably white.
zh: 我们 uncomfortably 地是白人。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were uncomfortably male and tried to change that.
zh: 我们 uncomfortably 地是男性,并试图改变这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a great business case for diversity.
zh: 多元化有很好的商业理由。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm really offended with this DEI thing that's going on now with the Trump administration.
zh: 我对现在特朗普政府搞的这套 DEI 的事真的感到被冒犯。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, we don't want DEI.
zh: 就像,我们不要 DEI。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, that's just nuts.
zh: 我是说,这简直是疯了。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was a business case for why DEI is a healthy thing.
zh: DEI 是一件健康的事情,这是有商业理由的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're programming, for example, to a diverse audience, why wouldn't you want to represent them?
zh: 比如说,如果你面向多元化的受众做节目编排,你为什么不想代表他们呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: And plus it's just healthier.
zh: 而且这样本来就更健康。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why do we want to just be a bunch of white guys?
zh: 我们为什么想变成一群白人男性呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't make any sense to me.
zh: 这在我看来毫无道理。

speaker: Unknown
en: We did have ended up about 50% women managers.
zh: 我们最终确实做到了大约 50% 的女性管理者。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it was particularly with African-Americans and Hispanics, we could just hire them and have them come on staff.
zh: 但尤其是非裔美国人和西班牙裔,我们可以雇用他们,让他们加入团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, you know, we could say, hey, we kind of look like that subway car that I always had in my mind we want it to look like.
zh: 然后,你知道,我们可以说,嘿,我们的样子有点像我脑海里一直想要的那节地铁车厢的样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if they didn't feel comfortable there,
zh: 但如果他们在那里感觉不自在,

speaker: Unknown
en: Then they end up leaving.
zh: 那他们最终会离开。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'd see these, they'd show me these numbers of what we have hired.
zh: 所以我会看到这些,他们给我看这些我们雇用了什么人的数字。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I go, oh, this is really good.
zh: 然后我说,哦,这真的很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're making improvement here.
zh: 我们在这里正在取得进步。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would actually make this a goal on people's bonus plans.
zh: 我实际上会把这个设为人们奖金计划里的一个目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: So after a couple of false starts, we got better at it.
zh: 所以在几次失败的尝试之后,我们在这件事上做得更好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We got better at trying to make the place comfortable for everybody.
zh: 我们在努力让这个地方对每个人都舒适方面做得更好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at the end, when I had left the company, we had achieved that.
zh: 到最后,当我离开公司时,我们已经实现了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was like in 2005, 2006.
zh: 那大概是 2005 年、2006 年的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd get in the elevators, I'd look around, I'd go, yeah.
zh: 我会走进电梯,我会环顾四周,然后说,嗯,是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We didn't.
zh: 我们没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I think it's a truism that homogenous teams tend to stay homogenous and teams that start diverse stay diverse.
zh: 我是说,我认为这是一个真理:同质化的团队倾向于保持同质化,而一开始就多元化的团队会保持多元化。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the corollary is you get what you measure and you get what you incentivize.
zh: 然后推论就是:你度量什么就得到什么,你激励什么就得到什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I very much share your concern about the attacks.
zh: 我非常认同你对这些攻击的担忧。

speaker: Unknown
en: DEI has become this like bad acronym and it's not...
zh: DEI 已经变成了一个像贬义缩写词的东西,而这并不是……

speaker: Unknown
en: Clear to me, I don't mean to be obtuse, but why?
zh: 对我来说不清楚,我不是有意装糊涂,但为什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, to your point, if we're serving diverse and representative populations, shouldn't we have teams that reflect those populations, if for no other reason?
zh: 就像,正如你所说,如果我们服务的是多元的、有代表性的群体,难道我们不应该拥有能反映这些群体的团队吗,哪怕没有别的原因?

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think there are a lot of other reasons to do this than to build the best business possible.
zh: 而且我认为这样做除了打造最好的企业之外,还有很多其他理由。

speaker: Unknown
en: What am I missing?
zh: 我遗漏了什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: What?
zh: 什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Nothing.
zh: 没什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: OK.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So is this racism and sexism?
zh: 那么这是种族主义和性别歧视吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's racism without the dog whistle.
zh: 这是没有暗号的种族主义。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's implicit racism all over the place in this.
zh: 这里面到处都充斥着隐性种族主义。

speaker: Unknown
en: As you look ahead as we're dealing with these challenges in our country, what gives you hope?
zh: 当你展望未来,面对我们国家正在应对的这些挑战时,什么给你带来希望?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I believe in the American people.
zh: 嗯,我相信美国人民。

speaker: Unknown
en: I believe this is really a dark time in many ways.
zh: 我相信这在很多方面确实是一段黑暗时期。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't detect a sense of optimism anymore.
zh: 我再也感受不到乐观的气氛了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I can't believe that that's not going to be back.
zh: 而且我不敢相信这种乐观不会回来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Despite everything that's going on in the world, many bad things, we still have probably the best system.
zh: 尽管世界上正发生着这一切，发生着许多坏事，我们拥有的可能仍然是最好的制度。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we do have checks and balances that haven't been demolished.
zh: 而且我们确实拥有尚未被摧毁的制衡机制。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really demoralizing to see the level of grift and graft and how spineless certain politicians are to accede to this happening.
zh: 看到如此程度的以权谋私和贪污腐败，以及某些政客在迎合这种现象时是多么没有骨气，实在令人沮丧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, it's not just politicians.
zh: 嗯，这不只是政客的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is something that I can't get my head around.
zh: 而且这是我一直无法理解的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as someone who spends time with, you know, CEOs and not just, you know, high flying private companies, but of public companies, we depend on rule of law.
zh: 作为一个花时间和 CEO 们相处的人——不仅是那些高飞的私营公司，还有上市公司——我们依赖法治。

speaker: Unknown
en: Rule of law is what allows business to thrive in America.
zh: 法治正是让商业在美国蓬勃发展的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we make a contract, we know that contract is going to be enforced and we can go to court and get a neutral ruling.
zh: 当我们签订一份合同时，我们知道这份合同会被执行，我们可以上法庭并得到中立的裁决。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the government's not going to come after one person or one company because they support the opposition party or the opposition candidates, right?
zh: 而政府不会因为某个人或某家公司支持反对党或反对派候选人就来找他们的麻烦，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: They haven't kowtowed to the current president.
zh: 他们没有向现任总统卑躬屈膝。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yet that's under attack right now.
zh: 然而现在这正受到攻击。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when you're talking with business leaders, are they even thinking about this?
zh: 那么当你和商业领袖们交谈时，他们甚至有在考虑这件事吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do they dismiss it?
zh: 他们对此不以为然吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do they think the threat is real?
zh: 他们认为威胁是真实的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: They would say the threat is real, but a lot of people are afraid to raise their hand.
zh: 他们会说威胁是真实的，但很多人都害怕站出来表态。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a collective action problem.
zh: 这是一个集体行动问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you go out alone, you're going to get your head chopped off?
zh: 如果你独自站出来，你的脑袋就会被砍掉？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how do we solve for that?
zh: 那么我们该如何解决这个问题呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: They're afraid to stand up.
zh: 他们不敢挺身而出。

speaker: Unknown
en: They've seen what has happened.
zh: 他们已经看到了发生过的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you have Tim Cook coming into the Oval Office with a gold gift for Trump, this reminds me, I spent a lot of time in third world countries, a lot of time in Africa, which I detail in the book, and I see this kind of cronyism and favoritism.
zh: 当你看到 Tim Cook 带着给 Trump 的金色礼物走进椭圆形办公室，这让我想起，我在第三世界国家待过很长时间，在非洲待过很长时间，我在书里详细写了这些，我看到的就是这种裙带关系和偏袒之风。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it's just, I mean, it's appalling.
zh: 我是说，这实在是，我是说，这令人震惊。

speaker: Unknown
en: But people
zh: 但是人们

speaker: Unknown
en: Think this is what you have to do to get things done in this administration and this is what my shareholders are going to need.
zh: 认为这就是你在这个政府里把事情办成所必须做的，这也是我的股东们所需要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they do it.
zh: 所以他们就这么做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they don't want to be singled out and have their head chopped off by
zh: 而他们不想被 singled out，被砍掉脑袋，被

speaker: Unknown
en: By Trump.
zh: 被 Trump 砍掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: This era of shareholder supremacy in running companies, this Milton Friedman concept that's not even 60 years old at this point, really minimizes stakeholders, whether that's customers and clients, that's team members, that is society at large, our nation at large.

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you see a path to elevating stakeholder interests in how companies are led?
zh: 你认为有没有一条路径可以提升利益相关者的利益在公司领导方式中的地位？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there a way back to a world where corporations have responsibilities that are co-equal with the shareholder responsibilities?
zh: 有没有办法回到一个企业责任与股东责任同等重要的世界？

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: We have really pretty much boiled it down to the shareholder interests.
zh: 我们确实几乎把它简化成了只看股东利益。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, it wasn't that long ago when companies would do these purposeful things.
zh: 而且，你知道，就在不久之前，公司还会做这些有目的性的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now they all got derided as, oh, this is woke stuff.
zh: 而现在它们全都被讥讽为，哦，这是 woke 那一套。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I hope it comes back.
zh: 所以我希望这种风气会回来。

en: I hope we're just going through a phase.

zh: 在我看来，这会是一个错失的机会。

zh: 我认为，如果人们不是害怕 somehow 这会被归入 woke 那个类别、你会因此受到攻击，会有更多的人去做这些事。
